title: Federal issues within state-law claims
summary: A narrow category of state-law claims can arise under federal law when resolving the claim necessarily requires deciding an actually disputed and substantial federal issue in a manner consistent with the federal-state division of judicial responsibility.
notes: The presence of a federal standard or the importance of the case to the litigants does not automatically satisfy the test. A hypothetical patent question in malpractice may matter greatly to the parties while lacking the required systemic significance.

sections.Meaning: A narrow category of state-law claims can arise under federal law when resolving the claim necessarily requires deciding an actually disputed and substantial federal issue in a manner consistent with the federal-state division of judicial responsibility.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the particular federal issue and why the state claim necessarily raises it. Ask whether it is disputed, substantial to the federal system rather than merely valuable to these parties, and appropriate for federal adjudication without upsetting the intended balance. Compare Grable with Gunn.
